items.stem: For a roadway, stopping sight distance generally:

options.rationale: Correct: higher speed means longer braking and reaction distance.
Faster vehicles need more, not less, distance to stop.
Stopping distance depends strongly on speed.
Pavement color is not a governing factor in stopping distance.

items.explanation: Correct: higher speed means longer braking and reaction distance.

items.stem: Superelevation on a horizontal curve is primarily provided to:

options.text: Help counteract the lateral (centripetal) demand of vehicles on the curve
options.rationale: Correct: banking offsets part of the lateral force needed to turn.

options.text: Increase the posted speed limit automatically
options.rationale: Superelevation is a design feature, not a legal speed change.

options.text: Drain water away from adjacent property only
options.rationale: Its primary purpose is lateral balance, not just drainage.

options.text: Eliminate the need for any side friction
options.rationale: It reduces but does not eliminate reliance on side friction.

items.explanation: Correct: banking offsets part of the lateral force needed to turn.

items.stem: Which TWO inputs most directly influence required pavement structural thickness?

options.text: The anticipated traffic loading (e.g., equivalent axle loads)
options.rationale: Correct: heavier/more traffic requires greater structural capacity.

options.text: The strength/stiffness of the subgrade soil
options.rationale: Correct: weaker subgrade requires a thicker structural section.

options.text: The color of the lane markings
options.rationale: Lane-marking color does not affect structural thickness.

options.text: The names of the adjacent streets
options.rationale: Street names have no structural relevance.
Speed limit by itself does not set structural thickness.

items.explanation: Correct keys: A, B. Correct: heavier/more traffic requires greater structural capacity. Correct: weaker subgrade requires a thicker structural section.
